sections.history: Vira Brahma, the shrine of the heroic Brahma, belongs to the nine Navabrahma temples that the Badami Chalukyas raised at Alampur on the Tungabhadra between the seventh and eighth centuries — Shiva temples all, though each bears a name of Brahma. It stands in the northern row of the group, between Arka Brahma and Vishwa Brahma, facing the site museum. The temple has been badly damaged over the centuries; it is no longer in worship and is today protected by the Archaeological Survey of India as part of the Alampur monuments.
sections.architecture: Vira Brahma follows the pattern that unites the Alampur group: an east-facing sanctum enclosed by a passage for circumambulation, entered through a hall, and crowned by a curving tower in the northern manner, its walls articulated with slender engaged pilasters. At the sanctum entrance two door guardians, dvarapalas, still keep watch, one of them heavily worn. High on the tower is a figure of Nataraja, Shiva as lord of the dance — an emblem fitting for a shrine whose name speaks of heroism and energy.
sections.legends: Vira means hero. The nine Navabrahma names are remembered at Alampur as the forms in which Brahma, performing penance on the banks of the Tungabhadra, worshipped Shiva; the god he adored is honoured here as Vira Brahmeshwara. For pilgrims the dancing Shiva on the tower is a reminder that the lord of stillness and meditation is also the lord of the cosmic dance.
sections.festivals: As a protected monument, Vira Brahma has no festival of its own. The precinct's living shrines carry the sacred year — Maha Shivaratri at Bala Brahmeshwara, and Navaratri and Dasara for the goddess Jogulamba — and visitors on those days find the whole compound full of pilgrims. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Look up before you step in: the Nataraja on the tower is easy to miss without a pause in the open court. At the doorway, the surviving dvarapala repays a close look at Chalukya carving at human scale. Vishwa Brahma, the best preserved of the northern row, stands next door, so the two are naturally seen together.

visit.timings: The Navabrahma precinct is open to visitors through the day; as an ASI-protected site, hours and any entry charges for the precinct and museum should be confirmed locally.
visit.dressCode: Modest dress is appreciated across the precinct, which includes living shrines; remove footwear where asked.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed at the monuments; tripods or professional shoots may need permission from the site authorities.
visit.gettingThere: Alampur is in Jogulamba Gadwal district, about 25 km from Kurnool and some 220 km south of Hyderabad, just off the Hyderabad–Bengaluru highway (NH 44). Alampur Road railway station, on the Hyderabad–Kurnool line, is about 9 km away; the temple stands within the Navabrahma precinct by the Tungabhadra, opposite the site museum.
